intent: "How is this doing?" — one measure set over one scope, grouped the way the question actually needs.
before_repeating: nothing at stake, but two runs are only the same number if as-of, window, basis, denominator and detection method all match.

input_schema.title: engagement.summarize input
input_schema.description: The provider's counts for one campaign over one window, one row per channel. The campaign is named as campaign.get names it.

external_id.description: The provider's own identifier, given to link a campaign for the first time. Later calls work by the pin.

window.description: Either a span, `from` and `to`, or one of the provider's presets. Both at once are refused, and so is neither: a window nobody chose is a number nobody can compare.

group_by.description: The one grouping this version offers: a row for each channel the provider reports.

external_ids.description: Only this plugin's own pins reach it, so another provider's identifier is never visible here.

envelope.description: What the numbers of this row count. Two rows are only the same number if all five match.

as_of.description: The plugin's clock when it asked, in UTC. The provider does not say when it counted.

window.description: The window exactly as it was asked for.

basis.description: The provider counted these; Jason counted nothing.

denominator.description: The count a rate of this row would divide by, where the provider names it; `unknown` where it does not.

detection.description: Whether an open, a reply or a bounce happened is the provider's judgement.

measures.description: The counts the provider reports for this channel. A count it does not report is absent, never 0, and no rate is ever returned.

overview.description: The block of the provider's answer this row was read from.

rows.description: One row per channel the provider reports, each with its own envelope.

campaign.description: The provider's identifier for the campaign this read summarised, pinned the first time as campaign.get pins it.

failure_codes.when: The provider holds no campaign under the identifier this call carried.
The provider account's plan or role does not include this capability, so no call by this account can answer it.
The provider refused the window, so no later attempt with the same window can answer.
The provider's answer was larger than this installation lets a plugin read from a program (`Plugins:Exec:OutputBytes`), so it was cut off; asking again would cut it the same way.
The vendor tool refused the call or never started, so nothing the operation asks for was ever attempted. Repeating it runs the same broken call.
The plugin's own credential does not let it read the counts of a campaign for this account.
The provider refused the read for now and it may be asked again.
The provider could not be reached, or answered with a failure on its own side.
The provider was called and no answer arrived. A read changes nothing and costs nothing, so the next attempt simply asks again.

conformance: A call carrying only `campaign.external_ids.campaign` answers, and a call carrying only `args.campaign.external_id` answers and returns that identifier under `external_ids.campaign`.
A campaign the provider does not hold fails `campaign_not_found` as permanent, rather than answering with no rows.
There is one row for each channel the provider reports, and none for a channel it does not; a row never mixes two channels.
A count the provider does not report is absent, never 0, and a rate is never returned: a rate is two counts and a denominator, and the envelope says which denominator is known.

Every row carries its envelope: `as_of` is the plugin's clock when it asked, `window` is the window exactly as asked, `basis` is `provider_reported`, `detection` is `provider`, and `denominator` is `unknown` unless the provider names the count its rates divide by.
A window the provider refuses fails `window_invalid` as validation, and is not asked again.
A read creates nothing and pins nothing but the campaign.
